name: Integrity
label: Victory
lede: It started as a fake band a Cleveland teenager invented on T-shirts, became the darkest, most metal thing on Victory Records with Charles Manson's blessing, and moved to Belgium because its singer fell in love on tour.

eras.title: A fake band made real
eras.text: Before Integrity existed, Dwid Hellion printed its merch. The teenager invented bands for fun, and one of them was billed as the most violent straight edge band alive. In 1988 he made it real in Cleveland, and its first album split hardcore down the middle.

years.h: Dwid Hellion: an Indiana farm, the blues and Thrasher
years.p: Dwid Hellion was raised by his grandparents on a farm near La Fontaine, Indiana, and fell for Delta blues and Alan Lomax's chain gang recordings. Skating, and Thrasher's music pages, led him to punk.

years.h: Dwid Hellion turns his invented band Integrity into a real one
years.p: After his youth crew band Die Hard broke up, Dwid Hellion recruited guitarist Aaron Melnick, drummer Tony "Chubby Fresh" Pines and bassist Tom Front, and gave them a name he'd already put on shirts.
years.xp:
As a teenager Hellion made up bands, designed their merch and spread their backstories. Integrity was pitched as a straight edge band so violent it would attack drinkers at shows. The logo came off the cover of a book called Integrity that he found in a secondhand shop.

Hellion told Thrasher the first members came out of a Cleveland skate crew called Team Playboy, and that the name Dwid itself came from a drunken slur of his own name.

years.h: A middle schooler takes over Integrity's bass
years.p: Tom Front quits after the Harder They Fall demo. Aaron Melnick's younger brother Leon, still in middle school, replaces him, and Chris Smith arrives from False Hope on second guitar.

years.h: Those Who Fear Tomorrow on Overkill Records
years.p: Integrity's debut bolts metal solos and chugging riffs onto hardcore. Critics warned it would ruin hardcore; it became a blueprint for metalcore, and Loudwire put it on its 2020 list of the top 25 metalcore albums.

eras.title: Holy terror on Victory
eras.text: With the Melnick brothers, Chris Smith and Mark Konopka, Integrity signed to Victory Records and made three albums in three years. The sound got bigger and stranger, and Dwid Hellion's world of doomsday cults, occult texts and Charles Manson moved to the center.

years.h: Integrity's Den of Iniquity EP
years.p: A stopgap between Integrity's Overkill debut and the Victory albums. The Hooked, Lung, Stolen Breath Cunt EP follows in 1994.

years.h: Mark Konopka of [[Outface|2fabef87-f53f-4792-b05b-6d54a8517d4c]] takes Integrity's drums
years.p: Tony Pines had left after the debut and David Nicholi Araca filled in. Mark Konopka, from the Cleveland band Outface, completes the line-up fans call classic Integrity.

yt: Dwid Hellion on why Systems Overload got remixed (Aggressive Tendencies)
years.h: Systems Overload: Integrity's Victory Records debut
years.p: The classic line-up's first album for Victory. Decibel inducted Systems Overload into its Hall of Fame in November 2013.
years.xp: Decibel's Hall of Fame story credits Chris Smith with helping write the material, and says [[Frank Novinec|b7befdca-a6f9-4440-8d24-95611017537a]] was around for the recording and joined soon after. The album was later remixed for its A389 Recordings reissue, which Dwid Hellion has explained on camera.

years.h: Frank Novinec joins Integrity after Systems Overload
years.p: Frank Novinec, later of Ringworm and [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]], comes in on guitar after the Systems Overload sessions. In 2006 he joins [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]], and he's still there two decades on.

years.h: Kids cut Dwid Hellion's mic cord; the whole room chases them
years.p: Aaron Melnick told Vice about a show where some kids cut Dwid Hellion's microphone cord. The room emptied out after them and they were chased down the street.

years.h: Charles Manson endorses Humanity Is the Devil
years.p: Integrity's second Victory album draws on the Process Church of the Final Judgement, and Charles Manson, writing to Dwid Hellion from prison, endorsed it. Manson's head went into the Integrity logo.
years.xp:
Hellion kept up a personal relationship with Manson, released recordings Manson made in prison, and has called him both a political prisoner and a religious martyr. Manson turns up again and again as a subject in Integrity songs.

Noisecreep reported speculation that Hellion, under the name Jack Abernathy, founded the Holy Terror Church of Final Judgment, a Process Church splinter group. Hellion hasn't confirmed it; he told Noisecreep many people treat the religion and the band as the same thing.

years.h: Seasons in the Size of Days: the last classic-era album
years.p: Integrity's third Victory album in three years, pulling in gothic rock, industrial and noise. The Melnick brothers, Chris Smith and Mark Konopka wouldn't record together again until 2013.

eras.title: Integ2000, then Brussels
eras.text: The classic line-up fell apart, and Dwid Hellion rebuilt Integrity with two members of Mushroomhead and a new name. Two more Victory albums followed, then Hellion moved to Belgium and took the band with him.

years.h: The Melnicks leave; Mushroomhead's Feltons make it Integ2000
years.p: With Aaron and Leon Melnick gone, Dwid Hellion hires brothers Dave and Steve Felton of Cleveland's Mushroomhead plus bassist Craig Martini, and renames the band Integ2000.

years.h: Integrity 2000 on Victory
years.p: The Integ2000 line-up's only album, out the same year as the Final Taste of Every Sin EP.

years.h: Closure, Integrity's fifth and last Victory album
years.p: With the Felton brothers gone, Dwid Hellion drops the Integ2000 name and closes out five straight Integrity albums on Victory. Invisible Oranges' Neill Jameson later heard a Southern Gothic streak in Closure.

years.h: Dwid Hellion moves Integrity to Belgium
years.p: Integrity relocated to Belgium in 2003. Hellion told Thrasher in 2018 why he'd lived in Brussels for about fifteen years: he met a girl on tour, they fell in love and married.

years.h: To Die For on Deathwish brings back Tony Pines
years.p: Sold as Integrity's comeback, To Die For is the band's first album on Deathwish Inc. and brings founding drummer Tony "Chubby Fresh" Pines back.

eras.title: The classic five, one more time
eras.text: Integrity came back from seven quiet years with a Deathwish album and a Manson single, both from Belgium. Then the Systems Overload line-up got in a room for the first time in two decades, for one night in Baltimore.

years.h: The Blackest Curse: Integrity's first album in seven years
years.p: Integrity's second album for Deathwish Inc., the label run by [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]]'s [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]], whose band is one of many that name Integrity as an influence.

years.h: Dwid Hellion releases a Charles Manson prison 7"
years.p: Dwid Hellion put out a new seven-inch of recordings Charles Manson made in prison on his own Holy Terror label, Noisecreep reported in May 2010.

years.h: Suicide Black Snake, and the old line-up starts recording
years.p: Integrity's ninth album comes out on A389 and Magic Bullet. The same year the Systems Overload line-up records its first new song together in more than twenty years.

years.cap: The Systems Overload line-up at A389 X Bash, Baltimore, 2014
years.h: The Systems Overload line-up plays again in Baltimore
years.p: Dwid Hellion, Aaron and Leon Melnick, Chris Smith and Mark Konopka play A389's tenth anniversary Bash, their first show together in more than seventeen years, and sell the new 7th Revelation EP weeks early.
years.xp:
A389's Domenic Romeo, guitarist in Pulling Teeth, had asked Aaron Melnick for years; Melnick told Vice he said no at first and that this was a one-time thing. A five-week tour was impossible with a two-year-old daughter at home. He and Leon were playing in the crossover band Inmates.

7th Revelation: Beyond the Realm of the VVitch came out officially on February 7, 2014. The show was later released as a live album, and Romeo joined Integrity's touring line-up.

eras.title: Francis Bacon, Relapse, and an old feud settled
eras.text: Integrity found a new home at Relapse Records with a line-up built around Dwid Hellion and drummer Alex Henderson. The records got more conceptual, the archive came out of the vault, and a 1990s grudge ended as a split record.

years.h: Howling: Francis Bacon at a séance, on Relapse
years.p: Integrity's tenth album follows the painter Francis Bacon, drunk at a séance in his studio at 7 Reece Mews, through occult moments in history. Dwid Hellion called it Integrity's most metallic record.
years.xp: Domenic Romeo added lap steel and solos Hellion likened to Randy Rhoads. Hellion told Bandcamp Daily he'd known Romeo about 20 years and that Romeo was close enough to tell him off.

q: I am a black sheep in hardcore.
years.h: Dwid Hellion's office full of Air Jordan 1s
years.p: Dwid Hellion wears only Nike Air Jordan 1s. His father once bought ten pairs at $10 each, which lasted him into his mid-twenties, and he now keeps boxes stacked to the ceiling.
years.xp: In the same Bandcamp Daily interview Hellion called himself a black sheep in hardcore, with no wish to conform.

years.h: Integrity split with black metal band Krieg on Relapse
years.p: Integrity shares a split EP with the American black metal band Krieg on Relapse Records, another step away from hardcore.

years.h: Relapse opens the vault: All Death Is Mine: Total Domination
years.p: A Relapse compilation of archival Integrity material, as Dwid Hellion keeps rotating guitarists: Asa Dunn joins in 2024 and Harley McCoy in 2025.

years.h: Integrity and Skarhead end a '90s feud with a split record
years.p: Dwid Hellion and Skarhead's Danny "Ezec" Singer had no love for each other in the 1990s. They started messaging, and the result is a split 12" on Static Era Records, with Integrity's Devil Down.
years.xp: No Echo reported the two bonded online by making jokes about Chubby Fresh of One Life Crew, the nickname of Integrity's own founding drummer Tony Pines. Hellion also sings on Skarhead's Till' Death We Part.
